stories.title: xAI sues a man for using Grok to generate CSAM ‘deepfakes’
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: xAI is suing an individual for allegedly using its Grok AI chatbot to create CSAM.
The lawsuit claims the user intentionally bypassed Grok's safeguards to generate and distribute illegal material.
This incident highlights ongoing challenges in AI safety, content moderation, and misuse of generative models.

stories.title: Third-party app stores coming to Google Play next week as Epic settlement withdrawn
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google Play will soon allow third-party app stores.
This change is a direct result of the withdrawal of a settlement.
Google is now subject to the full scope of antitrust remedies mandated by the court.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, emphasizing data privacy.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging existing local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing AI workloads on Macs.
This is presented as a preview, indicating ongoing development and performance improvements.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The key feature is running all AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Windows 0-day drops the same day Microsoft releases record number of patches
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical Windows 0-day vulnerability, named HiveLegacy, has been discovered.
The vulnerability is described as a 'powerful primitive' with potential for severe malicious use.
The discovery occurred concurrently with Microsoft releasing a large batch of security patches.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are advancing to the point of autonomously generating and submitting pull requests (PRs) to software projects.
The research shifts focus from individual PR outcomes to the broader adoption and management of these tools at the project level.
The study analyzes a large dataset of 25,264 agentic PRs across 2,361 popular GitHub repositories to investigate adoption patterns.

stories.title: Rethinking Penetration Testing for AI-Enabled Systems: From Resource Compromise to Behavioral Objective Violation
stories.author: Moslem Attar-Raouf
bullet_points: Traditional penetration testing is insufficient for AI-enabled systems.
New attack vectors target system behavior through manipulation of prompts, data, or inputs, rather than just infrastructure compromise.
The research proposes a shift in focus from resource compromise to behavioral objective violation in AI security testing.

stories.title: Early Adoption of Agentic Coding Tools by GitHub Projects
stories.author: Daqing Hou
bullet_points: Agentic coding tools are evolving to autonomously generate and submit pull requests (PRs) in software projects.
The research shifts focus from individual PR outcomes to how these tools are adopted and managed at the entire project level.
The study analyzes a large dataset of over 25,000 agent-generated PRs from popular GitHub repositories.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving support on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes functionality for web search capabilities in Claude Code.
This integration enhances the complexity and capability of AI agents running via Ollama.

stories.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
stories.author: Jie Li
bullet_points: Addresses the limitations of current LLM interaction when Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning fails.
Proposes a new method, 'Deep Interaction,' to improve efficiency in human-AI feedback loops.
Aims to overcome repetitive errors and the inefficiency of manual step-flagging by users.

stories.title: AI-accelerated End-to-End Framework for Rapid Professional Upskilling
stories.author: Robert Ogburn
bullet_points: Addresses the critical industry problem of slow enterprise skills gap closure amidst massive workforce reskilling needs by 2030.
Proposes a novel, end-to-end AI-accelerated framework covering five stages of knowledge acquisition and delivery.
Aims to improve upon existing frameworks by integrating AI across content development, teaching, and assessment verification.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how Transformer architecture components influence rank preservation across network depth.
Skip connections and normalization are reinterpreted not just for magnitude control, but as mechanisms to maintain gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard network operations (matrix multiplication, non-linear activations) inherently cause rank reduction.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether improvements from agent-optimization methods compound over time.
Current evaluations often treat optimization gains as one-shot, failing to model real-world, recursive deployment scenarios.
The research focuses on testing agent performance in a continual-learning setting using Terminal-Bench 2.0.

stories.title: The Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) Model and the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) in Autonomous Commerce
stories.author: Daya Shankar
bullet_points: The paper addresses the disruption of traditional customer loyalty models due to the rise of autonomous, goal-directed AI agents.
It introduces the Dynamic Verifiable Multi-Agent Human Agentic Loyalty Loop (DVM-HALL) model.
The research proposes the Net Human-Agent Score (NHAS) as a metric for evaluating human-agent relationships in autonomous commerce.

stories.title: Leveraging unlabelled data for generalizable neural population decoding
stories.author: Guillaume Lajoie
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of supervised learning in neural decoding for neurotechnologies like BCIs.
It introduces MOJO, a Masked Autoencoder-based approach to leverage unlabelled neural data for training.
The goal is to achieve robust and generalizable neural population decoding without requiring paired behavioral labels.

stories.title: MetaPerch: Learning from metadata for bioacoustics foundation models
stories.author: Jenny Hamer
bullet_points: Introduces 'MetaPerch,' a method to enhance bioacoustics foundation models using recording metadata.
Addresses the underutilized potential of readily available metadata (location, time) in large citizen science datasets like Xeno-Canto.
Aims to improve species detection models beyond what is achieved through supervision alone on large-scale audio data.

stories.title: Screening of Biosecurity Features in Metagenomic Data with Evo 2 Probes
stories.author: Vanessa Smilansky
bullet_points: The research explores using pre-trained genomic foundation models (Evo 2) for biosecurity screening without fine-tuning the large model.
Minimal linear and attention probes were trained on frozen Evo 2 activations to extract biosecurity-relevant signals.
The probes demonstrated strong discrimination in detecting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) within metagenomic data.

stories.title: Transforming Rank: How Architecture Navigates the Spectral Pathologies of Depth
stories.author: Katie Everett
bullet_points: The research analyzes how the Transformer feedforward block architecture influences the preservation of matrix rank across network depth during initialization.
It reinterprets skip connections and normalization not just as magnitude controllers, but as mechanisms specifically designed to maintain gradient rank.
The study demonstrates that standard expressive components (matrix multiplications, nonlinear activations) inherently reduce rank, and skip connections manage this trade-off.

stories.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
stories.author: Soheil Feizi
bullet_points: The paper investigates whether gains from agent-optimization methods compound over time.
Current reporting often treats optimization gains as one-shot improvements against a fixed benchmark.
The research addresses the critical real-world scenario where agents face recursive optimization due to new tasks and failures.

stories.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
stories.author: Ben Zhou
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'Hindcast,' a method to evaluate LLM forecasters by backtesting against prediction markets.
It identifies two major leakage issues in current LLM forecasting evaluations: retrieval models accessing post-event data and training data becoming too close to the prediction event.
The research highlights critical methodological flaws in how LLMs are currently being tested for predictive accuracy.

stories.title: Can an Old Dog Be Taught New Tricks? Taking LLMs Beyond Sentence Level Translation
stories.author: Alaina Brandt
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitation of current machine translation (MT) systems, which operate on a sentence-by-sentence basis.
It introduces PAT (Pragmatic Auto-Translator), a RAG-based system designed for whole-document, corpus-informed translation.
The system leverages context from comparable longform texts in U.S. English and Latin American Spanish, guided by user specifications.

stories.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
stories.author: Frederic Bechet
bullet_points: Introduces DeepStress, a new framework designed to stress-test deep search agents.
Addresses the gap in research regarding the robustness of search agents when faced with poor-quality evidence.
Simulates challenging evidence by replacing the retrieval module with a controlled synthetic environment.

stories.title: SPyCE: Skill-Policy Co-evolution for Multimodal Agents
stories.author: Weijie Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces SPyCE, a method for Skill-Policy Co-evolution in multimodal agents.
Addresses limitations of existing RL methods which force policies to relearn tool-use patterns from scratch.
Proposes a solution that integrates memory-based experience with policy updates to absorb reusable reasoning patterns.

stories.title: Post-Training Shifts Confidence: A Three-Stage Analysis of How SFT, RL, and OPD Shape Pre-, Intra-, and Post-CoT Calibration
stories.author: Xiaoyu Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how post-training methods (SFT, RL, OPD) affect the confidence calibration of LLMs during reasoning, moving beyond simple final-answer accuracy.

A novel three-stage calibration framework is introduced to analyze confidence at three distinct points: pre-CoT (difficulty estimation), intra-CoT (early termination), and post-CoT (answer aggregation).
This work addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by providing a granular view of how fine-tuning processes shape the model's internal certainty during complex reasoning tasks.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on LLM usage in kernel development
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds addressed the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the Linux kernel development process.
The discussion touches upon the integration and potential impact of AI tools in core operating system development.
The topic is highly relevant to systems programming, open-source development, and the future of software engineering.

stories.title: Post-Mortem: Building a Local MCP Server for Codebase Memory using Ollama and ChromaDB
stories.author: kike
bullet_points: Addresses developer concerns regarding cloud API billing and data privacy.
Details the implementation of a local Model Control Plane (MCP) server.
Leverages Ollama for local LLM hosting and ChromaDB for vector database management.
